items.title: Publish the core entity provenance and source-event contract
items.outcome: Every synced or exported financial entity carries one contracts-owned provenance component, so capture, offline sync, export and deduplication cannot invent incompatible source identifiers.
items.context: The source_event_id was added to the ingestion contract after the sync and export contracts were already scheduled, while api#17 separately claims to publish the candidate schema. Provenance crosses every language and repository and must exist before local persistence or sync.
scope: Opaque source_event_id generated and persisted before first enqueue
Entity id, source class, schema version, occurred and recorded instants, and optional provider reference
Separation from request idempotency keys, device-local raw-message HMACs and server dedupe fingerprints
Compatibility window for older clients that have no source_event_id
Generated Kotlin, TypeScript and Python types
Shared component consumed by capture, sync, export, import and audit contracts
acceptance_criteria: The component defines one source_event_id type and every consuming schema references it rather than declaring a local string
A raw_hash, message_digest or raw-content-derived identifier fails schema validation
The identifier remains stable across process death, retry and reinstall recovery from an encrypted queue backup
An old client without the field remains readable during the published compatibility window and no server synthesizes an identifier from raw text
Kotlin, TypeScript and Python round-trip the same generated fixture
api#17 and Android parser tickets no longer claim ownership of the schema
contracts_schema: OpenAPI 3.1 and JSON Schema provenance component with examples for manual, SMS, notification, import and API sources
security_privacy: The identifier is opaque, owner-scoped and carries no account, merchant or message content
The component structurally excludes device-local raw-message digests
observability: Contract requires provenance version and source class for mismatch metrics without source content
rollout_rollback: Publish additively before local persistence and sync implementation
Rollback preserves dual-read support for the prior schema until every queued old-client mutation expires
non_goals: Request idempotency semantics, which T-ADR-MONEY-01 owns
Cross-channel duplicate matching, which api#18 owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo contracts. Owns the provenance component and generated types; every producer and consumer references the published artifact without redeclaring fields.

items.title: Publish the natural-language transaction draft contract
items.outcome: AI service, core API and both clients share one typed transaction-draft, confidence and confirmation-token contract that cannot perform a write by itself.
items.context: T-AIP-05 currently publishes a cross-repository envelope from ai-service. The draft is consumed by Android, web and the normal transaction API, so service-local ownership would create three incompatible confirmation and expiry rules.
scope: Typed draft fields with per-field confidence and clarification reason
Opaque confirmation token bound to subject, draft hash, audience and expiry
Correction, cancel, expire and confirm state machine
Replay and conflicting-draft problem codes
Generated Kotlin, TypeScript and Python clients
Explicit absence of any direct transaction write operation
acceptance_criteria: Every field required by the ordinary transaction API is visible in the draft and low-confidence fields are distinguishable
The confirmation token is subject-, audience-, draft- and expiry-bound and is single use
Forged, expired, replayed and cross-subject tokens return stable problem codes with no ledger effect
No operation in the group can create, edit, delete, settle or pay a transaction
All three generated clients compile and pass the same state-transition fixtures
Outstanding drafts remain readable until expiry if new draft creation is disabled
contracts_schema: OpenAPI 3.1 draft group, closed state machine and RFC 9457 problem-code references
security_privacy: Original text retention is bounded and excluded from token contents, logs and analytics
Token verification is server-side and client correction never widens subject scope
observability: Requires state, expiry and refusal code without original text or amount
tests: Forged, expired, replayed and cross-subject token tests
rollout_rollback: Publish before T-AIP-05; creation remains disabled until all consumers pin the version
Rollback disables new drafts while existing drafts remain reviewable until expiry

Closed sort vocabulary and bounded page size
Unsupported combination and degraded-search problem codes
Generated Kotlin, TypeScript and Python clients

Unsupported filter and sort combinations return stable T-CON-12 problem codes

items.title: Govern human access to production data stores, backups and keys
items.outcome: No engineer, operator, CI principal or contractor has standing production data access; every break-glass session is time-boxed, second-approved, brokered, audited and visible to affected subjects.
items.context: Admin-console controls do not govern direct database, backup, object-store or KMS access. Monetary columns intentionally remain queryable integers, so an ungoverned human credential bypasses redaction, tickets, the audit chain and subject notification.
scope: Empty standing-access inventory for database, object and backup stores and KMS
Network-brokered, time-boxed elevation with independent approval and automatic expiry
Immutable eligible access basis originating from a user request, system incident or approved change record; operator-authored free text is never sufficient
Versioned roster with at least two independently eligible approvers, qualification evidence, expiry and on-call coverage; the requestor is excluded from the approval choice
Statement, object and key-use audit with actor, approval reference and row or object count
Projection into the foundational and tamper-evident administrative audit streams
FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY inventory for every user-scoped table
Subject-visible event for every unredacted human read
Restore and snapshot access under the same broker and scrub policy
acceptance_criteria: A scheduled IAM and database-role inventory fails unless standing human read grants are empty
Engineer workstation, developer identity and CI identity cannot connect directly or read backups
Elevation requires an eligible second approver, cannot be self-approved and expires automatically
The requesting operator cannot create, reclassify or approve the access-basis record, and an operator-originated support ticket is denied
If fewer than two eligible non-requesting approvers have current qualifications, new human production-data sessions remain disabled and the operator receives an escalation path rather than a bypass
Every successful human read has a correlated audit-chain entry before the session can close
Adding a user-scoped table without FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY fails the inventory check
An unredacted human read creates a subject-visible event without exposing operator identity
A restore to any environment runs the scrub and access checks before becoming available
contracts_schema: Machine-readable standing-access inventory, elevation record and broker-session audit schema using ADR-020 correlation identifiers
security_privacy: Broker credentials are short-lived, audience-bound and never issued to a workstation as reusable secrets
Audit records contain statement fingerprints and row counts, not copied financial rows
observability: Standing-grant count, elevation age, direct-connection denials, unaudited-session count and subject-event delivery
tests: Direct workstation, developer and CI access denial tests
Forged, operator-originated and provenance-reclassified access-basis denial tests
Expired qualification, requestor exclusion, approver absence and approver-roster fail-closed tests
Broker read with correlated audit and subject event
Backup and restore access denial tests
rollout_rollback: Enable before any environment contains real data
Rollback denies new human sessions; it never restores standing credentials
non_goals: Human-resources process beyond technical offboarding hooks
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo infra. Owns IAM, network broker and session audit integration; API supplies audit schemas and admin later renders review surfaces.
definition_of_done: Merged behind independent security review
Every acceptance criterion demonstrated in an isolated production-shaped fixture
Access inventory and denial tests are required checks
Break-glass and rollback rehearsal evidence recorded
Declared dependencies mirrored as native GitHub blockedBy edges

items.title: Prove user erasure survives backup restore and disaster recovery
items.outcome: A restore from a backup taken before erasure cannot resurrect a user's key or readable data, and a restore cannot complete while erasure tombstones remain unapplied.
items.context: Crypto-shredding destroys a wrapped user key in the live database, but point-in-time recovery can restore the pre-erasure key row and its ciphertext. Existing tickets only document this interaction and never execute the failure path.
scope: Independent append-only erasure tombstone journal outside the protected data backup window
Restore-time tombstone replay before environment readiness
Key re-destruction, blind-index cleanup and derived-store cleanup after restore
Restored-dataset execution of the T-SEC-02 erasure harness
Fail-closed behavior when the journal is unavailable
Idempotent replay and outstanding-tombstone alert
acceptance_criteria: Every erasure writes one immutable tombstone carrying opaque subject, key and erasure references
A restore is not marked complete until replay reports zero outstanding tombstones
A synthetic user erased after backup remains unreadable after that backup is restored
Disabling tombstone replay makes the planted restore test fail, proving the test detects resurrection
Blind-index and embedding or assistant-history residue queries return no match after restore
Replaying the same tombstone is idempotent and does not create a second record
Journal unavailability fails the restore rather than serving potentially resurrected data
contracts_schema: Versioned tombstone and replay-result schemas consumed by T-SEC-02, T-PLT-02 and release evidence
security_privacy: Tombstones contain no direct personal identifier or data value
The journal has independent retention, write-once policy and access controls
observability: Outstanding tombstones, replay age, failures and post-restore residue result
tests: Backup-before-erasure restore with planted readable-data failure
Blind-index, vector and conversation residue tests
rollout_rollback: Required in staging restore drills before beta
Rollback stops restore promotion; tombstone replay itself cannot be disabled in an environment with real data
non_goals: Primary erasure intake, which T-SEC-02 owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo infra. Owns independent tombstone storage and restore orchestration; API owns erasure and key destruction, and the shared harness verifies composition.
definition_of_done: Merged behind independent security and compliance review
Every acceptance criterion demonstrated by a performed restore
The planted resurrection test is shown failing before the control and passing after it
Restore evidence is consumed by the beta gate

items.title: Adopt the Android 16 API 36 behavior baseline
items.outcome: The Android baseline targets API 36 and explicitly handles Android 16 edge-to-edge, predictive back, large-screen, scheduling and stopped-state behavior before feature screens are built.
items.context: Google Play requires API 36 for submissions from 2026-08-31, while the stack document and estimates assume API 35. Android 16 removes layout opt-outs and changes job quota behavior that affects capture and sync.
scope: compileSdk and targetSdk 36 with pinned toolchain
Mandatory edge-to-edge insets on every root surface
Predictive-back integration and legacy callback removal
Large-screen orientation, resizability and aspect-ratio behavior
JobScheduler and WorkManager stop-reason and standby-bucket handling
Force-stopped and private-space tracking-paused detection and recovery
Developer-verification prerequisite for sideloaded QA
Standard Play Integrity request flow for protected server actions, with classic requests reserved only for documented highest-value actions
Restricted-settings matrix for Play-installed, sideloaded and restored builds covering notification-listener and other sensitive settings
acceptance_criteria: A Play-submittable build targets API 36 and no manifest or dependency lowers the effective target
All scaffold screens pass edge-to-edge and predictive-back tests on API 36
Six-hundred-dp and larger devices remain usable when orientation and aspect-ratio restrictions are ignored
Sync handles quota stop reasons without losing or duplicating queued transactions
After force-stop recovery the app shows tracking paused until capture health is restored
Sideloaded QA prerequisites are documented and executable
Standard Integrity tokens are bound to the intended request and replayed, expired, wrong-app and unlicensed verdicts fail closed; any classic-request use names its risk and quota budget
The restricted-settings matrix states what a sideloaded or restored build cannot enable and gives QA a supported recovery path without weakening production policy
API 31, 33, 35 and 36 behavior differences are recorded for T-QA-12
contracts_schema: Android platform-capability and capture-health state identifiers consumed by T-UX-01 and T-QA-12
security_privacy: Platform fallbacks never weaken encrypted storage, screen protection or permission scope
Tracking-paused state carries no transaction content
observability: API level, stop reason, standby bucket and capture-health state without device identifier or financial content
tests: API 36 target and manifest conformance test
Edge-to-edge, predictive-back and large-screen instrumented tests
Quota stop and queue durability tests
Standard Integrity binding, replay, stale-token and adverse-verdict tests
Restricted-settings matrix tests across Play install, sideload and restore paths
rollout_rollback: Land immediately after the Android repository scaffold
Target SDK cannot roll back below Play policy; regressions disable affected features rather than lower the target

items.title: Complete the Play Financial features declaration and permission classification
items.outcome: Every Play track carries an accurate Financial features declaration and the app uses only permissions allowed for its declared debt-management and financial-management categories.
items.context: Play requires all apps with financial features, including test tracks, to complete a Financial features declaration. The obligation matrix owns Data Safety and SMS declarations but not this separate classification, and the open QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES question is already answered by policy risk.
scope: Counsel-reviewed classification across financial management, advice, credit monitoring and other categories
Financial features declaration for internal, closed, open and production tracks
Permission inventory excluding QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, READ_CONTACTS, phone-number, broad media and fine-location access
Manifest queries allowlist for known payment apps
Android Contact Picker for invitations instead of broad contacts access
Evidence and re-declaration trigger on feature or permission change
Manual Play Console path where Publishing API cannot complete a declaration rollout
acceptance_criteria: Every active Play track shows a completed declaration matching current features
Counsel records whether debt calculators trigger accessory-credit restrictions and the app fails closed on unresolved classification
Manifest and dependency scans fail on QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, READ_CONTACTS and every prohibited permission
Known payment-app detection works through a narrow queries allowlist without installed-app enumeration
Split and family invitations use the Contact Picker or manual entry
A permission or financial-feature change invalidates prior evidence and blocks rollout until re-declared
The manual Console rollout path is rehearsed because the Publishing API cannot clear declaration alerts
contracts_schema: Machine-readable financial-feature category, permission inventory, declaration version and track evidence
security_privacy: No broad package, contact, phone, media or location inventory is collected
Declaration claims are reconciled against manifest and captured traffic
observability: Declaration age, track coverage, prohibited-permission findings and re-declaration requirement
tests: Prohibited-permission manifest and transitive dependency scan
rollout_rollback: Classification is resolved before any beta-track artifact is uploaded
Rollback removes the affected feature or permission; it never publishes under a stale declaration
non_goals: SMS permission declaration, which android#9 owns
Data Safety declaration, which T-CMP-03 owns
Credit bureau integration decision, which T-ADR-BUREAU-11 owns
